6 · Cut-away globe: a map and three sections in one object¶

The idea. A globe shows a field on its surface. Cut a wedge out of it (a range of longitudes, north of the Equator) and paint what lies below the surface on the three flat faces of the cut: two meridians and the equatorial plane. The reader sees a map and three vertical sections that meet at the right places, with no need to work out where each section lies.

This map. Annual-mean ocean temperature (World Ocean Atlas 2023) from the surface to 1000 m in the Pacific, cut along 180°, 110°W and the Equator.

Steps: 1 data → 2 one ray per pixel → 3 through the wedge to a face → 4 from the hit point to a value → 5 colour, light and lines → 6 the finished frame → 7 the animation.

CHANGE IF YOU LIKE — RUN
Settings

Everything you may want to change is in this one cell. The checks at the bottom stop the notebook with a plain message if a setting cannot work, before anything slow starts.

MODE = "FAST" (the default, one to three minutes; right for Google Colab) writes the poster at 1920 × 1080 px and a short preview clip of the animation at 960 × 540 px. MODE = "FULL" writes the poster at 3840 × 2160 px and the whole animation at 1920 × 1080 px (several minutes).

In [1]:
import os
import sys

MODE = "FULL" if "--full" in sys.argv else os.environ.get("GIS_MODE", "FAST")   # "FAST" (preview) or "FULL" (poster size, whole animation)
OUT_DIR = os.environ.get("GIS_OUT", "")          # output folder; "" = /content/out on Google Colab, ./out anywhere else
LON_WEST, LON_EAST = 180.0, 250.0                # the two meridians of the cut (degrees east): 180 and 110°W

from gismaps import nb                           # helpers: data loader, show(), video(), STOP checks, PASS / FAIL

nb.stop_unless(MODE in ("FAST", "FULL"), f"MODE = {MODE!r} must be FAST or FULL")
nb.stop_unless(0 <= LON_WEST < LON_EAST <= 360 and 30 <= LON_EAST - LON_WEST <= 120,
               "LON_WEST and LON_EAST must be degrees east, west face first, 30 to 120 degrees apart")
POSTER_SCALE = 1.0 if MODE == "FAST" else 2.0    # the design size is 1920 x 1080; the poster is saved at this multiple
OUT = nb.out_dir(OUT_DIR)
print(f"settings OK | mode: {MODE} | output folder: {OUT} | poster {int(1920 * POSTER_SCALE)} x {int(1080 * POSTER_SCALE)} px")

settings OK | mode: FAST | output folder: out | poster 1920 x 1080 px
RUN
1 · The data

Annual-mean ocean temperature from the surface to 2000 m on a 1° grid (World Ocean Atlas 2023, NOAA NCEI, public domain), reduced to one small file.

In [2]:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import cmocean

from gismaps.styles import common as C, cutaway      # the map-style code of this repository

data = nb.load("woa23_temperature")         # t_c100 (depth, lat, lon) in 0.01 degrees C; -9999 = no water
print("grid:", data["t_c100"].shape, "| depths:", data["depth_m"][0], "to", data["depth_m"][-1], "m")

grid: (34, 180, 360) | depths: 0.0 to 2000.0 m
RUN
2 · One ray per pixel

The camera is far away (parallel rays). For a pixel at (x, y), in Earth radii from the centre of the disc, the ray meets the unit sphere at the point P = x·right + y·up + sqrt(1 − x² − y²)·forward. Its longitude and latitude follow from P. If that point is outside the wedge, the pixel shows the surface.

RUN
3 · Through the wedge to a face

If the point is inside the wedge, there is no surface there: the ray flies on, in a straight line away from the camera, until it leaves the wedge. The wedge is bounded by three planes (meridian A, meridian B, the Equator), so the exit point is the nearest of three ray-plane intersections. That point has a radius between 0 and 1 and lies on one of the three faces.

cutaway.raycast does this for every pixel at once and returns what each pixel is and where its point lies.

In [3]:
rc = cutaway.raycast(600, lon_c=212, lat_c=30, lon_a=LON_WEST, lon_b=LON_EAST)
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(14, 4.6))
axs[0].imshow(rc["kind"], cmap="tab10", vmin=0, vmax=9); axs[0].set_title("what each pixel is: surface or one of three faces")
axs[1].imshow(rc["lat"], cmap="RdBu_r"); axs[1].set_title("latitude of the point seen")
axs[2].imshow(rc["rad"], cmap="viridis"); axs[2].set_title("radius of the point seen (1 = surface)")
for a in axs:
    a.axis("off")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
RUN
4 · From the hit point to a value

A face pixel knows its longitude, latitude and radius. Radius is turned into depth with a stated, linear scale: radius 1 is the surface and radius 0.5 is 1000 m. That is about 3,200 times deeper than true scale (1000 m is 0.016 % of Earth's radius), so the figure says "not to scale" in words. The temperature is then read from the atlas at (depth, latitude, longitude) by linear interpolation; where there is no water (land, sea floor) the face is grey.

In [4]:
globe = cutaway.OceanCutaway(data, lon_a=LON_WEST, lon_b=LON_EAST)
exaggeration = (1 - globe.R_IN) * 6371e3 / globe.zmax
print(f"depth exaggeration: about {exaggeration:,.0f} times")
depths = np.array([0, 100, 200, 300, 500, 1000.0])
rad = 1 - depths / globe.zmax * (1 - globe.R_IN)
for name, lo in (("west face", LON_WEST), ("east face", LON_EAST)):
    t = globe.interior_t(np.zeros_like(rad), np.full_like(rad, lo), rad)
    print(f"Equator at {name:12s}:", "  ".join(f"{d:.0f} m {v:4.1f}" for d, v in zip(depths, t)), "(deg C)")

depth exaggeration: about 3,186 times
Equator at west face   : 0 m 28.6  100 m 27.6  200 m 16.0  300 m 11.3  500 m  8.2  1000 m  4.5 (deg C)
Equator at east face   : 0 m 24.3  100 m 14.8  200 m 12.8  300 m 11.8  500 m  8.1  1000 m  4.6 (deg C)

The numbers show what the equatorial face tells: at 180° the water is still about 28 °C at 100 m, while at 110°W it is about 15 °C at the same depth, some 13 degrees colder. The warm layer is deep in the west and shallow in the east.

RUN
5 · Colour, light and lines

Surface and faces share one colour bar (cmocean.thermal, −2 to 30 °C). The sphere is shaded as a ball; each face gets one brightness from its angle to the light, so the three faces can be told apart. Dark lines on the faces mark every 5 °C, white arcs every 250 m, and a light outline separates the parts.

In [5]:
img = globe.globe(700, lon_c=212, lat_c=30)
plt.figure(figsize=(7.5, 7.5), facecolor=C.BG); plt.imshow(img); plt.axis("off"); plt.show()

Clipping input data to the valid range for imshow with RGB data ([0..1] for floats or [0..255] for integers). Got range [0.0..1.000000003808644].

poster = globe.poster(OUT / "cutaway_globe.png", scale=POSTER_SCALE)
nb.show(poster)
RUN — A SHORT PREVIEW IN FAST MODE, THE WHOLE ANIMATION IN FULL MODE
7 · The animation

Three moves, the same every time this device is used: the whole globe turns to the place, the wedge opens (meridian B swings east from meridian A), then labels fade in while the camera sways a few degrees so that the faces separate in depth.

In [7]:
if MODE == "FULL":                               # the whole animation, 1920 x 1080 px
    movie = globe.animate(OUT / "cutaway_globe.mp4", OUT / "frames_06")
else:                                            # a short preview: every 10th frame, 960 x 540 px, 12 frames a second
    movie = C.preview(globe.animate, OUT / "cutaway_globe_preview.mp4", OUT / "frames_06", thin=10)
nb.video(movie)
RUN — PASS OR FAIL FOR EVERY OUTPUT
Check the outputs

The last cell checks that every output exists and is what it should be, and prints PASS or FAIL per check.

In [8]:
size = (int(1920 * POSTER_SCALE), int(1080 * POSTER_SCALE))
checks = [
    ("the poster exists", poster.exists()),
    (f"the poster is {size[0]} x {size[1]} px", nb.image_size(poster) == size),
    ("the ray-cast found the surface and all three faces", len(np.unique(rc["kind"])) >= 4),
    ("depth is exaggerated (and the figure says so)", exaggeration > 100),
]
if not os.environ.get("GIS_PART"):               # (GIS_PART marks a frame worker of the parallel FULL render)
    checks.append(("the movie exists and is not empty", movie is not None and movie.exists() and movie.stat().st_size > 20_000))
nb.verify(checks)

PASS - the poster exists
PASS - the poster is 1920 x 1080 px
PASS - the ray-cast found the surface and all three faces
PASS - depth is exaggerated (and the figure says so)
PASS - the movie exists and is not empty
